name: AD8610 / AD8620
tagline: ADI's trimmed 6 nV/√Hz, 25 MHz JFET: an OPA627-class pick for DAC filters and portable headphone amps.

lineage.note: Sole source. One combined datasheet (AD8610_8620.pdf); copyright line suggests 2001. Tangentsoft reviewed it by 2005.

part_numbers.note: SOIC-8, A grade, leaded. Probably discontinued under PDN 10_0081 Rev. B; still on Octopart.
SOIC-8, A grade, RoHS, −40 to +125 °C. Newark 60AK7654 (ARZ-REEL7).
SOIC-8, B grade (~100 µV). BRZ believed active (Newark 59K6944); leaded BR likely discontinued.
MSOP-8, A grade, reels only (ARMZ-REEL: Farnell 1424175). ARMZ believed active; ARM likely discontinued.

part_numbers.pn: AD8620AR / AD8620AR-REEL / AD8620AR-REEL7 / AD8620ARZ / AD8620ARZ-REEL / AD8620ARZ-REEL7
part_numbers.note: Dual SOIC-8, A grade (Farnell 9994386). In the FiiO X7 MkII AM3A. ARZ believed active.
Dual SOIC-8, B grade (~100 µV). BRZ believed active; leaded BR likely discontinued.

key_specs.value: 60 V/µs typ (a parts DB says 50 V/µs)
±5 V to ±13 V (abs max 27.3 V or ~27 V total)
±30 mA (parts DB); stable into >1 nF, all gains

key_specs.source: ADI Op Amp Applications Handbook ch. 3

key_specs.value: Trimmed JFET input ('the very best trimmed JFET')

reputation.summary: Popular with Head-Fi and diyAudio rollers since the mid-2000s. Tangentsoft (Warren Young) calls it a favourite, especially for battery amps: like the AD823 minus some aggressiveness. ADI's AN-1429 lists the AD8620 among parts 'reputable with music fans'. Used in Topping NX5 (with BUF634), Xuelin iHiFi990 (DAC LPF) and FiiO X7 MkII AM3A.
typical_uses: Headphone gain stage with BUF634 buffer (Topping NX5)
caveats: Specified only ±5 to ±13 V (abs max ~27 V total); not a drop-in for ±15 V rails.
SOIC/MSOP only (dual SOIC only); DIP sockets need an adapter.
±30 mA output; low-impedance headphones usually need a buffer (BUF634 in the Topping NX5).
Tangentsoft advises against aggressive or bright systems. No ASR or Samuel Groner THD+N data found.
Battery use (Tangentsoft): 5.7 V total swings 0.5 V into 33 Ω; 7.6 V swings 2.0 V into 330 Ω.

counterfeit_notes: AD8610 is MSOP-8/SOIC-8 only and AD8620 SOIC-8 only, so a native DIP-8 or MSOP 'AD8620' is suspect. SOIC parts on DIP adapters are legitimate. Marketplace DIP fakes are reported, unconfirmed. Check the ADI marking; buy from authorized distributors.

part_numbers_affected: other AD8610/AD8620 orderables (full list not read)
silicon_changes.identification: Not visible in the marking. Trace by ADI date code or lot against the PCN effective date.
silicon_changes.summary: ADI PCN 26_0028 qualifies its Limerick, Ireland fab (ADLK) for XF26/XF18/XF12/XF8 process products, leveraging an existing qualified process for supply continuity. AD8610 and AD8620 orderables are reportedly listed. Same die and part numbers; whether this is a move or an added fab is unknown.

spec_deltas.before: previous fab for XF-process products (not named in the sources seen)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: None documented. ADI states no fit, form, function or reliability impact; no comparative measurements found.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low – same part numbers and datasheet; only lot provenance changes.
silicon_changes.verification: PCN scope confirmed; AD8610ARZ-REEL7, AD8610BRZ, AD8620ARZ reportedly listed. A conflicting 28 Sep 2025 effective date was discarded.

silicon_changes.identification: Not visible in the marking; use a date code after the PCN effective date.
silicon_changes.summary: After Sumitomo discontinued certain mold compounds, ADI changed mold compound, and sometimes die-attach, for SOT23, MiniSO, MQFP, PDIP, PLCC, SOIC, SSOP and TSSOP packages. AD8610/AD8620 variants are reportedly listed. Package materials only; die unchanged.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low – package-material change; same die and pinout.
silicon_changes.verification: Rev. E form and parts list found; part rows not seen.

silicon_changes.identification: Date code after the PCN effective date. The die is unchanged.
silicon_changes.summary: PCN 10_0004 moves SOIC narrow-body assembly at Amkor to a halogen-free mold compound, with no stated fit, form, function or reliability impact. AD8610/AD8620 variants are reportedly listed.
silicon_changes.verification: PCN content confirmed on other parts; AD8610/AD8620 listing reported only.

silicon_changes.identification: None. The difference is only in the test site, traceable through the lot.
silicon_changes.summary: ADI qualified TeamQuest Technology Inc. as an additional test site for TC-Vos (offset-drift) testing to secure continuity of supply. The TC-Vos test process itself is unchanged. The die, assembly and data sheet are unchanged.

spec_deltas.after: existing site(s) plus TeamQuest Technology Inc.

silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low – test-site addition only; same die and datasheet.
silicon_changes.verification: PCN content confirmed; AD8610 orderables itemized.

silicon_changes.identification: Country of origin and lot/date code on MSOP parts assembled at Amkor Philippines. No top-mark change is stated.
silicon_changes.summary: ADI added Amkor Philippines as an alternate assembly site for 8/10-lead MSOP and MSOP_EP to secure supply. It states no expected change to device functionality, fit, form or reliability. The AD8610 is among the listed products. This is an assembly-site change only.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low – alternate assembly site only; affects only the MSOP version.
silicon_changes.verification: PCN confirmed: Amkor Philippines MSOP site, March 2021, AD8610 listed.

open_questions: Is Rev. F (2009) still current? What changed from Rev. D to F, and when were A–C issued?
Which XF process do these parts use, and which orderables does PDN 10_0081 Rev. B discontinue?
Abs max 27.3 V or 27 V? At what supply is 60 V/µs specified? Confirm e_n frequency, i_n, Iq, THD+N.
Was there a separate single-channel AD8610 datasheet first? Does ADI call the trim DigiTrim? Confirm offset-null pins.
Independent measurements (ASR, Samuel Groner) wanted; Head-Fi, Leckerton, diyAudio and Zigsow claims need re-reading.
